title: Losing the Night
instructions: You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: For almost the whole of human history, a clear night meant a sky crowded with stars. Today, according to an atlas of night-sky brightness compiled from satellite measurements in 2016, more than eighty per cent of the world's people live under skies polluted by artificial light, and about a third can no longer see the Milky Way from their homes. The change has been so gradual that few have noticed it. When an earthquake cut the electricity supply to Los Angeles in 1994, some residents reportedly telephoned emergency services to describe a strange silvery cloud overhead. They were seeing the Milky Way for the first time.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: Astronomers were the first to protest, since the glow above cities makes faint objects impossible to observe; major observatories have long since retreated to remote mountains and deserts. But in recent decades biologists have shown that the consequences reach much further. Life on earth evolved under a dependable cycle of light and darkness, and a great many species use it to regulate their behaviour. Many are active only after dark, when they feed, mate or migrate under cover of night, and for them a lamp that never goes out is as great a change to their surroundings as the felling of a forest.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: The best-known victims are sea turtles. Hatchlings emerging from nests on a beach find the sea by heading for the brightest horizon, which under natural conditions is the one over the water. Where a beach is lined with hotels and street lamps, they crawl inland instead and die of exhaustion or are killed on roads. Migrating birds, many of which travel at night, are drawn towards illuminated towers and circle them until they collapse or collide with the glass. Insects gather in such numbers around lamps that they are easily picked off by predators, and since insects pollinate plants and feed countless other animals, their losses pass along the food chain.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Humans are not exempt. Exposure to light in the evening, particularly light with a strong blue component, delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that prepares the body for sleep. Researchers have linked disturbed sleep to a range of health problems, although how much of the blame belongs to outdoor lighting, as opposed to screens and indoor lamps, is uncertain. People who work night shifts, whose exposure is greatest, have been the subject of particular study. What can be said is that much outdoor light serves no purpose at all. By some estimates, around a third of it shines upwards or sideways, illuminating nothing that anyone needs to see, at a cost of billions in wasted electricity.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: The arrival of light-emitting diodes, or LEDs, was expected to help, because they use far less energy than older lamps and can be aimed precisely. In practice, the result has often been the opposite. Because LED lighting is so cheap to run, towns have tended to install more of it and to leave it on for longer. The white LEDs first chosen for streets are also rich in blue light, which scatters more widely in the atmosphere. The old sodium lamps they replaced, for all their inefficiency, gave an orange glow that travelled less far. A study based on tens of thousands of observations by volunteers concluded in 2023 that the night sky had been growing brighter by nearly ten per cent a year – much faster than satellites, which are relatively insensitive to blue light, had indicated.

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: Unlike most forms of pollution, this one can be reversed at the flick of a switch, and it leaves no residue. The town of Flagstaff in Arizona, home to an important observatory, has restricted outdoor lighting since 1958 and remains noticeably darker than other towns of its size. The measures it uses are simple: lamps are shielded so that they point only downwards, warmer colours are preferred, and lights are dimmed or switched off late at night. Elsewhere, stretches of countryside have been declared dark-sky reserves, in which lighting is strictly controlled and to which visitors travel specifically to see the stars. France introduced national rules on similar lines in 2019. Fears that darker streets invite crime and accidents are understandable, but a large study of local authorities in England and Wales that had reduced their street lighting found no evidence of an increase in either.

groups.instruction:
Reading Passage 2 has six paragraphs, A–F.
Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below.
groups.limit: Write the correct number, i–ix, next to Questions 14–19.

options.i: A technology that has not delivered the expected benefit
options.iv: A problem with a straightforward cure
options.v: A loss that has gone largely unnoticed
options.vii: From a specialist complaint to a wider concern
options.viii: Consequences for human health and a needless expense
options.ix: The stars as an aid to navigation

groups.instruction:
Look at the following effects of artificial light (Questions 20–22) and the list of animals below.
Match each effect with the correct group of animals, A, B or C.
groups.limit: Write the correct letter, A, B or C, next to Questions 20–22.

items.text: They become easy prey for other animals.
They set off in the wrong direction soon after they are born.
They fly round and round tall structures.

groups.limit: Choose ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage for each answer.

rows.text: Evening light with a strong blue component delays the release of a hormone called {23}.
It is estimated that about a {24} of outdoor light is wasted because it shines upwards or sideways.
The 2023 study of sky brightness relied on observations made by {25}.
Flagstaff has had restrictions on outdoor lighting since {26}.

questions.explain:
答案是 v。A 段說大多數人已經活在光害的天空下，而 The change has been so gradual that few have noticed it；洛杉磯居民停電時認不出銀河的例子也在說明這一點。
同義轉換：few have noticed it ＝ gone largely unnoticed。
questions.quote: The change has been so gradual that few have noticed it.

questions.explain:
答案是 vii。B 段說最先抗議的是天文學家，But 近幾十年生物學家發現影響範圍大得多。
陷阱：vi 也提到 observatories，但 B 段只說天文台搬到偏遠地區，完全沒談經費。
questions.quote: But in recent decades biologists have shown that the consequences reach much further.

questions.explain:
答案是 ii。C 段舉了三種動物：小海龜爬向內陸、候鳥被亮著燈的高塔吸引、昆蟲聚集在燈旁。
解題關鍵：led astray 是「被引入歧途」的意思，概括了三個例子的共同點。
陷阱：ix 提到 navigation，但文章沒有談用星星導航。
questions.quote: Where a beach is lined with hotels and street lamps, they crawl inland instead

questions.explain:
答案是 viii。D 段前半談光對人體的影響（延後褪黑激素分泌、睡眠受干擾），後半談約三分之一的戶外光毫無用處，浪費數十億的電費。
同義轉換：serves no purpose / wasted electricity ＝ a needless expense。
questions.quote: What can be said is that much outdoor light serves no purpose at all.

questions.explain:
答案是 i。E 段說 LED was expected to help，但 In practice, the result has often been the opposite：因為便宜，反而裝得更多、開得更久。
同義轉換：was expected to help... the opposite ＝ has not delivered the expected benefit。
questions.quote: In practice, the result has often been the opposite.

questions.explain:
答案是 iv。F 段第一句就說這種污染 can be reversed at the flick of a switch，接著用 Flagstaff 的例子說明 The measures it uses are simple。
陷阱：iii（街燈的歷史）不對。1958 是 Flagstaff 開始限制照明的年份，不是在講街燈的發展史。
questions.quote: Unlike most forms of pollution, this one can be reversed at the flick of a switch

questions.explain:
答案是 C（昆蟲）。昆蟲大量聚集在燈旁，they are easily picked off by predators。
同義轉換：easily picked off by predators ＝ become easy prey for other animals。
questions.quote: Insects gather in such numbers around lamps that they are easily picked off by predators

questions.explain:
答案是 A（海龜）。Hatchlings（剛孵化的小海龜）本來朝最亮的地平線走就能找到海，海灘有燈光時 they crawl inland instead。
同義轉換：hatchlings emerging from nests ＝ soon after they are born；crawl inland instead ＝ set off in the wrong direction。
questions.quote: Hatchlings emerging from nests on a beach find the sea by heading for the brightest horizon

questions.explain:
答案是 B（候鳥）。候鳥 are drawn towards illuminated towers and circle them，一直繞到力竭或撞上玻璃。
同義轉換：circle ＝ fly round and round；towers ＝ tall structures。
questions.quote: are drawn towards illuminated towers and circle them until they collapse or collide with the glass

questions.explain:
答案是 melatonin（褪黑激素）。原文 delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that prepares the body for sleep。
解題關鍵：題目的 a hormone called 對應原文逗號後面的同位語說明。
questions.quote: delays the release of melatonin, the hormone that prepares the body for sleep

questions.explain:
答案是 third（三分之一）。原文 around a third of it shines upwards or sideways。
解題關鍵：空格前已經有 a，只填 third。A 段也有 about a third，但那是指看不到銀河的人口比例，和這題無關。
questions.quote: around a third of it shines upwards or sideways, illuminating nothing that anyone needs to see

questions.explain:
答案是 volunteers（志願者）。這項研究 based on tens of thousands of observations by volunteers。
陷阱：不要填 satellites。衛星測到的增加速度比較慢，是拿來和這項研究對比的。
questions.quote: A study based on tens of thousands of observations by volunteers concluded in 2023

questions.explain:
答案是 1958。Flagstaff has restricted outdoor lighting since 1958。
陷阱：2019 是法國實施全國性規定的年份。
